nodes.title: CLIP：语言监督的图文对齐
nodes.summary: CLIP：语言监督的图文对齐
nodes.definition: CLIP learns a shared embedding space from image–text pairs by distinguishing matching captions from mismatches. An image encoder and a text encoder are trained jointly, and candidate class descriptions can then act as zero-shot classifiers through similarity comparisons. This changes the interface from a fixed classifier vocabulary to textual descriptions. The global training objective can overlook spatial relations or fine details within long captions. A robot can use CLIP features for grounding, but action selection and physical feedback require additional mechanisms.
nodes.example: Encode a robot image and several descriptions such as a red cup and a blue bowl. Rank their similarities, then inspect whether changing a spatial relation changes the score appropriately. Image–text ranking alone does not specify a grasp pose or feasible action.
nodes.role_en: Uses natural-language descriptions for downstream queries. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

notation.meaning: One-direction schematic; CLIP also aligns in the reverse direction.

nodes.title: Depth Anything V2：合成教师与真实图像蒸馏
nodes.summary: Depth Anything V2：合成教师与真实图像蒸馏
nodes.definition: Depth Anything V2 improves monocular depth using a large teacher trained with synthetic supervision and student models trained through pseudo-labeled real images. This uses synthetic labels for geometric detail while exposing students to real-image diversity. The released models span different capacities and include metric-depth adaptations with additional labels. Relative depth and metric distance must remain distinct when a robot consumes the output. Its practical inference is a feed-forward depth map; converting that map into safe navigation or grasping requires calibration and a downstream control system.
nodes.example: Run a relative-depth model on a cup beside a table and inspect boundary quality. Before treating values as meters, confirm that the chosen checkpoint is metric and matches the camera convention. Compare error on transparent or reflective objects separately from ordinary textured surfaces.
nodes.role_en: Produces efficient per-pixel depth. Course-associated reading for Visual Representation of Depth and 3D.

nodes.title: VGGT：联合预测相机、深度与三维结构
nodes.summary: VGGT：联合预测相机、深度与三维结构
nodes.definition: VGGT is a feed-forward Transformer that jointly predicts several three-dimensional scene quantities from one or more images. Its outputs include camera parameters, point maps, depth, and point tracks. Learning these quantities together provides geometry-aware features useful beyond an isolated reconstruction task. Unlike a pipeline that optimizes every new scene from scratch, the trained network directly infers a reconstruction. Nevertheless, camera conventions, scale, correspondence quality, and static-scene assumptions must be checked before using its predictions as a robot map or simulation asset.
nodes.example: Provide several views of a room and compare predicted camera poses and point maps in a common frame. Reproject points into the images to inspect consistency, then test downstream use separately; a visually plausible cloud can still contain metric or occlusion errors.
nodes.role_en: Supports reconstruction and other spatial tasks. Course-associated reading for Visual Representation of Depth and 3D.

nodes.title: HydroShear：有历史状态的触觉剪切仿真
nodes.summary: HydroShear：有历史状态的触觉剪切仿真
nodes.definition: HydroShear models tactile force and shear using a non-holonomic hydroelastic contact formulation. It tracks interaction history so that stick-slip transitions and accumulated shear depend on the path of contact rather than only the instantaneous indentation image. Signed-distance geometry supports contact with varied watertight shapes. The simulator aims to reproduce signals useful for control, not merely photorealistic sensor appearance. The authors evaluate tactile fidelity and transfer of reinforcement-learning policies, keeping the sensor-model comparison and the downstream task outcome as distinct evidence.
nodes.example: Press and then slide an object across a tactile surface. Compare simulated and measured shear buildup and release before training a task policy. Two sensor images that look similar may still encode very different forces and slip behavior.
nodes.role_en: Tests whether realistic signals improve hardware control. Course-associated reading for Robot Learning from Multimodal Experiences for Dexterity.

nodes.title: DINO 自蒸馏
nodes.summary: 用缓慢更新的教师指导学生学习跨视图稳定的视觉特征。
nodes.explain:
DINO让学生看一张图的不同裁剪视图，去匹配教师对相关视图产生的分布。教师参数并非用同一损失直接反传更新，而是学生参数的指数移动平均，变化较慢，提供较稳定目标。输出还结合中心化与温度等设计，避免所有输入的分布退化成同一种答案。这里的“蒸馏”不要求先有一个人工标注训练的大教师；教师在训练过程中与学生共同演化。应分别画出数据流、梯度流和参数更新流，才能理解stop-gradient为什么重要。DINO学的是视觉表示，不是动作条件动力学；之后仍需另外训练世界模型预测这些表示怎样随动作变化。

例如同一张图的全局视图能看到箱子与桌面，局部视图只看到箱子边缘；学生需要从局部获得能与教师目标一致的信息。不能要求不重叠且内容无关的所有裁剪天然有相同语义，因此视图采样规则是训练方法的一部分。
nodes.symbols: λ：移动平均系数；p：经温度softmax得到的输出分布；教师分支停止梯度。
nodes.role: DINOv2与DINO-WM的方法背景；教师学生不是ID-WM两层规划的同义词。
nodes.pitfall: 教师用普通梯度下降和学生同时更新；DINO本身就是世界模型。
nodes.quiz: 教师慢更新的作用是什么？
nodes.answer: 提供较稳定的学习目标；但避免坍缩还依赖其他设计。

notation.meaning: Teacher and student output distributions for related views; centering and temperatures are method components.

nodes.definition: DINO trains a student network to match the output distribution of a teacher on different views of an image. The teacher parameters are updated by an exponential moving average of the student rather than by its own backpropagated matching loss. Output centering, sharpening, and multi-view training are important parts of the method, not optional explanations of a plain agreement objective. Its self-distillation setup learns useful visual representations without human class labels for the pretraining examples.
nodes.example: For a teacher distribution \((0.8,0.2)\) and a student distribution \((0.5,0.5)\), the cross-entropy is \(-0.8\log0.5-0.2\log0.5\). Student gradients change the output toward the teacher target. After a student update, the moving-average rule changes teacher parameters gradually. These output categories are learned representation coordinates and should not automatically be interpreted as named human object classes.
nodes.role_en: DINO is methodological background for DINOv2 and frozen visual features. Its teacher/student pair is unrelated to ID-WM’s high-level/low-level planning hierarchy: those two world models have different prediction targets rather than a teacher-student distillation objective.

paper.contribution: Self-distillation without labels learns visual representations using student and momentum-teacher predictions.

nodes.title: DINOv2 视觉特征
nodes.summary: 以改进目标、数据和训练配方，学习可迁移的图像与patch表示。
nodes.explain:
DINOv2在DINO思想基础上结合图像级和patch级学习等训练设计，并强调大规模数据整理和训练稳定性。对下游研究者，它像一个已经学会提取图像结构的测量仪：输入画面，输出全局或空间特征。冻结它可以减少下游训练负担，并让当前、预测和目标处于固定的特征坐标中。但特征距离不是由物理单位定义的距离，背景变化、视角、纹理和小物体都可能影响它。机器人任务必须验证特征是否保留位置、接触和目标差异。DINOv2不是DINO-WM：前者提供视觉编码，后者另外训练动作条件的特征预测器，再用规划找动作。

可把原图和patch特征的二维网格并排展示，用特征相似度查询一个区域在另一张图的对应位置。这比仅用最终分类准确率更贴近操作任务。遇到视角大变或遮挡，匹配可能失败，不能从漂亮特征可视化推断可靠三维几何。
nodes.symbols: oₜ：观测图像；E：预训练编码器；zₜ：patch或全局特征，需明确选哪一种。
nodes.role: DINO-WM使用冻结DINOv2 patch特征；ID-WM视觉路线建立在视觉表征预测基础上。
nodes.pitfall: DINOv2直接输出机器人关节角；特征欧氏距离等于真实米数。
nodes.quiz: 为何规划时要编码目标图像？
nodes.answer: 把目标放入与预测状态相同的特征空间以计算代价。

nodes.definition: DINOv2 is a family of pretrained visual encoders developed through large-scale self-supervised training. It extends the DINO line with training and data improvements, including both image-level and patch-level objectives. Spatial patch representations can be reused for tasks that need local image structure. Freezing the encoder preserves a fixed target representation during downstream dynamics learning, but neither freezing nor pretraining guarantees complete physical state information or invariance suitable for every control task.
nodes.example: Encode two images of the same tabletop before and after a push. Each image yields a grid of patch features. A world model can learn to predict the later grid from earlier features and an action sequence, while a goal image supplies a target grid. Changes in viewpoint, lighting, and object geometry may affect feature distances differently, so their relation to task success requires evaluation.
nodes.role_en: DINO-WM predicts frozen DINOv2 patch features rather than training the transition model to reconstruct every pixel. This representation choice supports visual planning and forms background for ID-WM’s visual model branch; it is not needed for the state-only experiments.

paper.contribution: Data curation and scaled self-supervised training produce broadly useful visual features.

nodes.title: DINOv3：保持稠密特征的自监督视觉
nodes.summary: DINOv3：保持稠密特征的自监督视觉
nodes.definition: DINOv3 scales self-supervised visual representation learning and addresses degradation of dense patch features during long training. Its Gram anchoring objective preserves relationships among patch embeddings using a reference representation. The relevant Gram matrix compares patches, so it should not be described as a generic channel-correlation constraint. The released model family also uses data curation, large-scale optimization, and post-training adaptations for resolution, size, and text alignment. Its output is a visual representation rather than an action or explicit dynamics transition.
nodes.example: Compare patch-similarity matrices before and after extended training, then evaluate both image-level recognition and dense prediction. A stronger global classification score alone does not show that object boundaries or patch correspondences were preserved.
nodes.role_en: Provides visual representations for other tasks. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.title: MAE：遮挡像素重建
nodes.summary: MAE：遮挡像素重建
nodes.definition: MAE learns an image encoder by reconstructing missing pixels from a heavily masked image. The encoder sees only visible patch tokens, while a smaller decoder combines their representations with mask tokens to predict the missing content. This asymmetry reduces pretraining computation and makes high masking ratios practical. The reconstruction task supplies supervision without category labels. After pretraining, the decoder is usually discarded and the encoder supports downstream tasks. Pixel reconstruction and semantic feature prediction are different objectives even when both use masking.
nodes.example: Mask most patches in an image of a table, encode the visible patches, and reconstruct the hidden ones. For robot control, retain the encoder and separately train the policy; successful reconstruction is not evidence that the policy understands which object to grasp.
nodes.role_en: Defines the self-supervised target. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.title: VideoMAE：视频管状遮挡重建
nodes.summary: VideoMAE：视频管状遮挡重建
nodes.definition: VideoMAE extends masked autoencoding to spatiotemporal video tokens. Tube masking hides corresponding spatial regions across time, reducing the possibility of recovering a masked patch by copying an adjacent frame. High masking ratios exploit video redundancy while leaving a challenging reconstruction task. The encoder learns from visible tokens and the decoder reconstructs missing video content. The method is a representation pretraining approach, not an action-conditioned simulator; downstream action recognition and robot control require their own inputs, objectives, and evaluation.
nodes.example: If one patch is hidden in only one frame, its neighboring frames may reveal the same texture. Hide the spatial tube across several frames and compare learned action-recognition features, while keeping training and evaluation video splits separate.
nodes.role_en: Supplies a self-supervised learning target. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.title: VideoMAE V2：双重遮挡与规模化
nodes.summary: VideoMAE V2：双重遮挡与规模化
nodes.definition: VideoMAE V2 reduces both encoder and decoder cost through dual masking. The encoder receives one subset of video tokens and the decoder processes a further selected subset rather than reconstructing every token with the same computational burden. This permits larger video encoders and broader pretraining. A progressive training strategy combines diverse video sources with later task-oriented training. The change concerns scalable representation learning; it does not turn reconstructed videos into an action-conditioned physical simulator or a direct robot control policy.
nodes.example: Compare two pretraining runs with the same video encoder but different decoder token counts. Measure memory and throughput alongside downstream recognition. A faster decoder is useful only if the resulting encoder retains the visual and temporal distinctions needed by the task.
nodes.role_en: Transfers representations to downstream tasks. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.definition: NEPA trains a vision Transformer to predict subsequent patch embeddings from preceding embeddings. nodes.role_en: Learns features transferable beyond the pretext task. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.title: SigLIP：图文匹配的成对Sigmoid损失
nodes.summary: SigLIP：图文匹配的成对Sigmoid损失
nodes.definition: SigLIP replaces the globally normalized contrastive softmax objective with a pairwise sigmoid objective for image–text matching. Each pair contributes according to whether it matches, so loss normalization no longer requires the same global similarity distribution as CLIP. This changes scaling behavior, batch-size tradeoffs, and the treatment of positive and negative pairs. It still learns visual and textual representations rather than a direct policy. The practical value to robotics lies in the resulting visual backbone and grounding features, with task-specific control trained separately.
nodes.example: Create a batch with matching and mismatching image–caption pairs and compare their individual sigmoid losses with a softmax-normalized contrastive loss. Vary the negative-to-positive ratio while evaluating transfer, because larger batches alone do not establish better robot features.
nodes.role_en: Supplies transferable vision-language features. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.summary: CAFT：局部与整体图文对齐
nodes.definition: CAFT addresses image–text models that match the dominant scene but neglect details in long captions. Its fine-to-coarse image encoder and part–whole text encoder learn local phrase-region agreement at intermediate stages together with final global alignment. This creates a useful bridge from global vision-language retrieval to spatially grounded representations, while detailed robot action grounding remains a separate downstream question.
nodes.example: Compare captions that share the same scene but differ in a small object attribute or relation. Examine both retrieval scores and the image regions associated with the changed phrase. A correct global match should not hide failure to ground that detail.
nodes.role_en: Connects phrase-region detail to whole-scene matching. Course-associated reading for Visual Representations of Images and Videos.

nodes.definition: DynaMo pretrains visual representations on in-domain robot observations using a dynamics-related predictive objective before imitation learning. Predictive representation learning therefore improves the policy’s input rather than automatically providing an explicit planner or a pixel-generating world simulator.

The design is important when reading later depth foundation models, which can reuse related decoder ideas with very different training data.

nodes.definition: VGGT-Ω studies scaling feed-forward reconstruction for static and dynamic scenes. The architectural change concerns how views exchange information and how outputs are decoded; it does not make all reconstructed geometry physically accurate without validation.

Performance depends on both supervisor guidance and the actor’s ability to execute it, so language correctness and complete physical recovery should be measured separately.

The underlying policy still learns or executes the actual robot action mapping.

nodes.definition: ViTaSCOPE fuses vision and tactile observations in an object-centric implicit representation. It represents object geometry with a signed distance field and tactile feedback through neural shear fields, then estimates the in-hand object pose and external contact locations. The two sensing modalities provide complementary evidence when the hand occludes an object or when contact cannot be inferred from images alone. Simulation supports scalable learning and transfer. Its estimated object/contact state is an input to manipulation reasoning, not itself a dexterous action policy.

nodes.title: ADEPT：灵巧控制预训练与稳定后训练
nodes.summary: ADEPT：灵巧控制预训练与稳定后训练
nodes.definition: ADEPT pretrains a dexterous policy on general object reposing and post-trains it for harder downstream manipulation. Stable adaptation combines behavior-cloning distillation, critic warm-up, and conservative on-policy updates to avoid erasing the useful pretrained behavior. A joint-space Geometric Fabric mediates between the policy and the robot, while perceptive students learn from teachers. The framework demonstrates visuo-tactile control on multiple high-degree-of-freedom embodiments. Pretraining reuse, control mediation, and teacher–student transfer are separate components whose contributions should be read independently.
nodes.example: Start a new manipulation task from a challenging object orientation. Compare training from scratch, naive fine-tuning, and the stable post-training recipe using identical task distributions. Check whether the original reposing capability survives and whether the perceptive student transfers to hardware.

nodes.title: 单目深度、尺度与稠密预测
nodes.summary: 单目深度、尺度与稠密预测
nodes.definition: A depth map assigns a distance-related value to each image pixel. A monocular predictor estimates it from learned visual cues, which generally do not determine absolute scale without additional assumptions or calibration. Relative-depth models can order surfaces while differing in scale or shift; metric models require a metric training or calibration convention. Depth also differs from a complete three-dimensional map because occluded surfaces are unobserved. Dense depth predictions can feed reconstruction, grasping, or navigation, but errors at object boundaries and reflective surfaces need explicit evaluation.

nodes.summary: 多视图几何与对应关系
nodes.definition: Multi-view geometry relates image observations of the same scene through camera intrinsics, poses, and three-dimensional structure. Correspondences connect pixels that observe the same point, while projection maps a world point into each camera. Reconstruction jointly estimates some of these unknowns and depends on sufficient viewpoint variation and consistent image evidence. Neural methods may predict cameras and geometry directly, but the coordinate and scale ambiguities still matter. A geometrically consistent reconstruction is useful for robot perception and scene memory; it is not automatically a contact-valid simulator asset.

nodes.title: 有符号距离场
nodes.summary: 有符号距离场
nodes.definition: A signed distance field represents a surface as the zero level set of a scalar function over three-dimensional coordinates. The magnitude describes distance to the boundary, and the sign distinguishes inside and outside under a declared convention. Neural implicit models approximate this function with trainable parameters. Surface normals can be derived from spatial gradients when the function is regular. In robot perception, an SDF can combine visible geometry with contact constraints, but the representation alone does not specify mass, friction, elasticity, or a dynamically valid collision model.

nodes.definition: A Gaussian scene representation stores many spatial primitives with means, covariances, opacity, and appearance attributes. Projecting and compositing them renders an image, allowing map parameters and camera poses to be fitted to observations. Robotics extensions attach semantic or latent features and update the map from streaming sensor data. The representation supports efficient rendering and differentiable optimization, but rendered appearance does not by itself establish watertight geometry or physical material properties. Tracking, map expansion, feature storage, and dynamic-object handling remain separate algorithmic design choices.

nodes.summary: 逆渲染与逆物理参数估计
nodes.definition: Inverse rendering estimates scene parameters that could have produced observed images. Inverse physics extends the unknowns to motion, initial state, contacts, and material or dynamics parameters. A renderer and simulator predict observations, and optimization reduces the mismatch with recorded data. Multiple parameter settings can explain similar images, so identifiability and additional constraints are central. Joint optimization can reduce error propagation but also become unstable; staged or sensitivity-based optimization changes the problem. Estimated visual fidelity and accurate future physical prediction should be evaluated separately.

nodes.definition: Tactile sensors measure local interaction with an object through deformation, force, pressure, shear, or images of a deformable sensing surface. Simulating attractive tactile images does not guarantee realistic forces or shear. Contact-rich learning therefore needs both sensor-model validation and complete closed-loop task evaluation.

nodes.definition: A scene graph represents entities as nodes and their relationships as edges. Spatial graphs can store object position, containment, support, identity, and semantic attributes; dynamic graphs also track change through time. This makes previously observed information explicit when the current camera view is incomplete. Building the graph requires perception, association, and update rules, while a downstream policy or reasoning model decides how to use it. A compact symbolic relation may omit uncertainty or detailed geometry, so graph correctness and task success need separate tests.

nodes.definition: An affordance describes an action or interaction that an object or scene permits relative to an agent and a task. nodes.definition: Robot memory preserves information from earlier observations or experiences that may be necessary for a current decision. Retrieval-based systems store entries and select relevant ones using a query, while recurrent or attention-based systems compress history into a state or context. nodes.definition: An informative action is chosen partly for what it reveals about unknown state or parameters. Experimental design formalizes this by optimizing an uncertainty or sensitivity criterion rather than collecting arbitrary repetitions. In contact-rich manipulation, useful information depends on whether and how contact excites the unknown physical parameters. Fisher information measures how strongly an observation likelihood changes with parameters under a model. High information in a model does not guarantee successful identification when that model is misspecified, so subsequent estimation accuracy and task performance still require measurement.

nodes.title: 图像联合嵌入预测架构
nodes.summary: Predict semantic image-region embeddings from context without pixel reconstruction or negative pairs.
nodes.definition: I-JEPA learns image representations by predicting target-region features from visible context-region features. The target branch encodes the image and supplies stop-gradient representation targets; a predictor uses context and target-position information. Large target blocks and informative distributed context encourage semantic prediction rather than merely interpolating nearby pixel texture. The objective predicts representations rather than reconstructing pixels or contrasting against a set of negative examples. This is a representation-learning paper, not yet an action-conditioned robot dynamics model.
nodes.example: Hide several image blocks while leaving spatially distributed context visible. The context encoder and predictor estimate the target encoder features at the hidden positions. Matching these vectors trains useful image features. No robot action enters this image-only training example, so a controller cannot obtain motor consequences merely by running the encoder.
nodes.role_en: I-JEPA provides the representation-prediction foundation for later video JEPAs and action-conditioned predictive models. It should remain distinct from the full control loop.

notation.meaning: Predictor. The displayed loss summarizes target-feature matching.

nodes.summary: Combine large-scale action-free pretraining and smaller robot interaction data for latent planning.
nodes.definition: V-JEPA 2 first learns action-free video representations at large scale, then supports action-conditioned latent world modeling through V-JEPA 2-AC. The post-trained predictor takes robot interaction context and actions to predict future visual embeddings. Goal-image planning compares predicted and target features, enabling action selection without requiring generated RGB futures. The pretrained encoder and action-conditioned model are distinct stages. The paper robot results concern particular Franka manipulation tasks and deployment settings, not arbitrary hardware or complete physical simulation.
nodes.example: Encode the current camera view and a goal image of an object at the desired location. For several candidate robot-action sequences, predict future embeddings with the action-conditioned predictor. Select actions whose features approach the goal and reobserve after execution. The action-free encoder alone cannot perform this candidate-action prediction.
nodes.role_en: This is the central JEPA-family bridge from internet video pretraining to robot planning. Its goal-distance planning gives a concrete comparison to DINO-WM and ID-WM.

nodes.summary: HODOR：面向任务的物体层级表示
nodes.definition: HODOR organizes visual representations hierarchically around objects and object parts, allowing a robot task to select relevant combinations rather than using one undifferentiated scene vector. The hierarchy is a representation design, not a complete symbolic planner; the downstream policy still needs demonstrations and closed-loop evaluation.

nodes.title: ForageBench：需要物理交互的家庭目标搜索
nodes.summary: ForageBench：需要物理交互的家庭目标搜索
nodes.definition: ForageBench evaluates finding and retrieving a language-specified object in an unfamiliar house-scale environment. Targets may be occluded, so navigation alone is insufficient: manipulation can be needed to reveal the evidence required for search. Its PhyGS simulation framework combines procedural environments, photorealistic appearance, physical interaction, and low-level robot control. The contribution is a benchmark and evaluation setting rather than a single universal policy. Success depends on coordinating spatial memory, object search, and contact-capable execution.

nodes.definition: DSRL adapts a diffusion policy by learning how to choose its latent noise input. The base behavior-cloning policy can remain fixed, while reinforcement learning changes the distribution of generated actions through this lower-dimensional interface. The method requires black-box access to the policy rather than gradients through all of its weights. This separates policy steering from ordinary parameter fine-tuning and seeks data-efficient real-world improvement. Exploration quality and the reachable action manifold still constrain what the fixed base policy can achieve.
nodes.example: Keep a pretrained diffusion policy frozen and compare random noise with noise selected by the learned steering policy. Evaluate improvement using the same physical task and interaction budget; a better steering distribution cannot guarantee actions outside the base policy’s coverage.
nodes.role_en: Optimizes task return over noise choices. Course-associated reading for Robots That Learn from Experience.

nodes.definition: Posterior Behavioral Cloning studies which imitation-learning initialization makes later reinforcement learning effective. The proposed approach models uncertainty about the demonstrator’s behavior given the dataset rather than only fitting a single action estimate. nodes.definition: SplaTAM uses three-dimensional Gaussians as an explicit map for dense RGB-D simultaneous localization and mapping. A Part Layout Adapter encodes conditions, while a two-stage diffusion process first generates layout-aligned geometry and then decomposes it into the specified meshes. nodes.summary: GAINS：稀疏视图的高斯逆渲染
nodes.definition: GAINS estimates geometry, materials, and lighting from sparse multi-view captures using Gaussian-based inverse rendering. A first stage stabilizes geometry with learned depth, normal, and diffusion priors. A later stage uses segmentation, intrinsic decomposition, and additional priors to regularize material recovery. These constraints address ambiguities where appearance can be explained by several combinations of shape, reflectance, and illumination. The recovered parameters support relighting and rendering, but physically meaningful interpretation depends on the rendering model and available views.
nodes.example: Fit the same object from few views and inspect both geometry and estimated material. Relight it under an unseen illumination and compare with held-out captures, because matching the training images alone can hide incorrect reflectance or lighting.
nodes.role_en: Separates appearance explanations using additional constraints. Course-associated reading for From Pixels to Physics: Understanding and Manipulating Physics from Images.

nodes.definition: ProJo4D estimates deforming geometry, appearance, physical state, and material properties from sparse multi-view video. Instead of fitting each variable permanently in sequence or optimizing everything at once, it progressively enlarges the jointly optimized set according to sensitivity. This permits later physical evidence to refine earlier geometry while avoiding some instability of a fully coupled problem from initialization. A differentiable visual-physical model links observed images to future predictions. Its main contribution is the optimization schedule and coupling, rather than a generic neural-video generator.

nodes.role_en: Expands coupled variables to reduce error propagation. Course-associated reading for From Pixels to Physics: Understanding and Manipulating Physics from Images.

nodes.definition: HarmoVid harmonizes foreground-video lighting with a target background while preserving temporal consistency. This distinction matters for robotics data preparation: natural-looking illumination does not establish correct object geometry, material identification, or contact behavior.
nodes.example: Place a foreground portrait into a changed scene and inspect both individual frame lighting and flicker across the whole video. Compare the full pipeline with its stage ablations instead of treating a good still image as sufficient video evidence.
nodes.role_en: Maintains coherence across frames. Course-associated reading for From Pixels to Physics: Understanding and Manipulating Physics from Images.

nodes.summary: Cloak：遮掉末端执行器以促进跨本体迁移
nodes.definition: Cloak masks the robot’s own end-effector from the wrist-camera view during VLA training and deployment. The mask is rendered from known robot geometry rather than inferred by a segmentation or generative model, and augmentation varies its extent during training. The intent is to prevent appearance-specific visual shortcuts tied to the source gripper. The action and kinematic interfaces still need a meaningful cross-embodiment mapping; hiding hardware appearance does not by itself solve differences in reach, contact mechanics, or available actions.
nodes.example: Train using one gripper while masking its wrist-view appearance, then test an unseen gripper or hand under the declared action mapping. Compare source performance and target transfer, and inspect whether object pixels were accidentally removed by the mask.
nodes.role_en: Defines deployment on different robot hardware. Course-associated reading for Learning Human and Robot Motions.

Its benefits are evaluated inside downstream view synthesis, stereo, and Gaussian reconstruction tasks.

nodes.title: MEM 多尺度具身记忆
nodes.summary: Combine visual short-term and language long-term memory for sustained robot tasks.
nodes.definition: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory equips a VLA with short-horizon visual history and longer-horizon abstract language memory. The short-term encoder preserves recent motion and interaction information, while language records task progress and relevant events beyond the raw-image window. The method jointly reasons about what to do and what to retain. Memory helps partial observability but can introduce causal confusion if irrelevant past information creates spurious shortcuts. The system therefore addresses a specific architectural and training problem rather than assuming that unlimited context automatically improves robot control.
nodes.example: During kitchen cleanup, an object can leave the camera view after being placed in a drawer. A recent image window no longer contains the event, but a textual memory can retain that the drawer contains the object and that this subtask is complete. Incorrect memory must still be corrected by new evidence.
nodes.role_en: MEM extends VLA policies with task memory and connects history windows to long-horizon reasoning. It remains separate from updating a simulator state or training a predictive world model.

nodes.explain: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory equips a VLA with short-horizon visual history and longer-horizon abstract language memory. The short-term encoder preserves recent motion and interaction information, while language records task progress and relevant events beyond the raw-image window. The method jointly reasons about what to do and what to retain. Memory helps partial observability but can introduce causal confusion if irrelevant past information creates spurious shortcuts. The system therefore addresses a specific architectural and training problem rather than assuming that unlimited context automatically improves robot control.
nodes.role: MEM extends VLA policies with task memory and connects history windows to long-horizon reasoning. It remains separate from updating a simulator state or training a predictive world model.

nodes.title: MemER：从经历检索关键帧来控制机器人
nodes.summary: MemER：从经历检索关键帧来控制机器人
nodes.definition: MemER uses a high-level policy to select and track relevant earlier keyframes instead of feeding every past observation indiscriminately to the controller. The high-level model combines retrieved experience with recent frames and generates instructions for a low-level action policy. This creates an explicit interface between long-horizon memory and execution. The paper adapts existing vision-language and VLA backbones rather than claiming a memory mechanism alone solves control. Retrieval correctness, instruction quality, and final manipulation success should be evaluated separately.
nodes.example: After a minutes-long task, require an action that depends on an earlier event. Inspect which frame is retrieved and whether it actually contains the needed evidence, then test the low-level action rather than scoring only the generated instruction.
nodes.role_en: Executes the memory-conditioned instruction. Course-associated reading for Memory for Robotics.

nodes.title: MemoryVLA：感知认知记忆与扩散动作
nodes.summary: MemoryVLA：感知认知记忆与扩散动作
nodes.definition: MemoryVLA separates current perceptual/cognitive tokens from a persistent memory bank holding detailed and semantic information. Current working representations retrieve relevant stored entries, fuse them with present observations, and update the bank by consolidating redundant content. A memory-conditioned diffusion action expert then predicts an action sequence. This explicit cognition–memory–action organization targets tasks where the current image is insufficient. Human-memory terminology motivates the design, but its effectiveness rests on the actual storage, retrieval, update rules, and task evidence rather than a biological equivalence.
nodes.example: Hide an object after the robot has observed it and ask for a later action requiring that earlier state. Inspect retrieved entries, compare with memory disabled, and test whether consolidation loses a detail that the task still needs.
nodes.role_en: Generates memory-conditioned action sequences. Course-associated reading for Memory for Robotics.

nodes.title: RoboMME：系统评估机器人策略的记忆
nodes.summary: RoboMME：系统评估机器人策略的记忆
nodes.definition: RoboMME is a standardized benchmark for history-dependent robot manipulation. Its task taxonomy separates temporal, spatial, object, and procedural memory, and a suite of memory-augmented VLA variants enables controlled comparison. This tests whether a policy actually uses required history rather than merely accepting more input frames. Different representations can benefit different tasks, so one overall score should not erase those distinctions. The benchmark is an evaluation framework, not evidence that every tested memory mechanism generalizes to unrestricted long-horizon operation.
nodes.example: Use one task requiring repeated-action counting and another requiring an occluded object’s identity. Compare the same base policy with different memory designs and inspect per-category results, because a representation useful for spatial recall may fail procedural counting.
nodes.role_en: Tests memory representations and integration strategies. Course-associated reading for Memory for Robotics.

nodes.title: PALM：交互可供性与连续任务进度
nodes.summary: PALM：交互可供性与连续任务进度
nodes.definition: PALM combines interaction-oriented affordance representations with continuous within-subtask progress prediction for long-horizon manipulation. Distilled cues describe object relevance, contact geometry, spatial placement, and motion dynamics, providing task-relevant anchors for the policy. Progress signals help decide when to continue or transition rather than repeating or prematurely ending a step. The design connects representation learning to execution sequencing. A predicted progress value is still an estimate, so transitions should be checked against physical task completion instead of trusting internal confidence alone.
nodes.example: In a multi-step task, compare the predicted progress with actual object state before a transition. Remove affordance or progress cues separately to test whether failures come from selecting the wrong interaction or switching at the wrong time.
nodes.role_en: Uses these cues to execute and transition. Course-associated reading for World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation.

nodes.title: T-REX：高频触觉反应式灵巧操纵
nodes.summary: T-REX：高频触觉反应式灵巧操纵
nodes.definition: T-REX adds temporal, high-frequency tactile processing to learned manipulation policies. A tactile-rich dataset emphasizes elementary motor primitives, while a temporal tactile VQ-VAE encodes changing touch signals. A variable-rate mixture-of-Transformers architecture combines those signals with other modalities without forcing every stream to the same frequency. This addresses dynamic contact rather than treating touch as one static image. The method’s benefit should be assessed on force-sensitive and deformable interactions, keeping sensing bandwidth, action rate, and task success distinct.
nodes.example: During a delicate contact task, compare temporal tactile encoding with a static tactile image under matched data. Check whether the controller reacts to changing slip or force, and report actual sensor and action rates instead of assuming a high-rate encoder guarantees high-rate physical response.
nodes.role_en: Supports force-sensitive manipulation. Course-associated reading for World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation.

nodes.title: DreamZero：联合视频与动作的世界动作模型
nodes.summary: DreamZero：联合视频与动作的世界动作模型
nodes.definition: DreamZero builds a World Action Model on a pretrained video diffusion backbone and jointly predicts visual futures and robot actions. Video provides a dense learning target for how scenes evolve, while the action output supports robot execution. System optimizations make the large generative backbone usable in a closed loop under the reported control setting. The framework also studies transfer from video-only demonstrations and limited new-embodiment data. Joint prediction does not automatically make generated futures physically calibrated or remove the need for feedback and deployment-rate measurement.
nodes.example: Compare a model trained only on action imitation with joint video–action prediction under matched robot data. Evaluate task generalization, actual closed-loop rate, and failure rollouts rather than treating high-quality predicted video as proof of successful control.
nodes.role_en: Replans from actual observations rather than trusting an entire imagined rollout. Course-associated reading for World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation.

nodes.title: VTAM：高效的视频触觉动作联合模型
nodes.summary: VTAM：高效的视频触觉动作联合模型
nodes.definition: VTAM adapts a pretrained video backbone to model both visual and tactile futures, then adds an action expert trained from task demonstrations. RGB and tactile observations share a frozen video VAE and pretrained Transformer weights, while a lightweight tactile-flow force proxy provides an additional learning signal. The action path avoids full iterative video denoising at inference, improving latency. This distinguishes using generative training signals from requiring every deployment step to render a future video. Transfer claims remain tied to the tested sensor and robot interfaces.
nodes.example: Compare training with and without future tactile targets, then measure actual action latency with video denoising disabled. Evaluate contact success separately from predicted tactile appearance, including changes in sensor type and task initialization.
nodes.role_en: Produces actions without full video denoising. Course-associated reading for World-Action Models for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation.

nodes.title: DAViD：视频生成与三维人类物体交互
nodes.summary: DAViD：视频生成与三维人类物体交互
nodes.definition: DAViD learns dynamic human–object affordances by synthesizing interaction videos and lifting them into four-dimensional training examples. A human motion diffusion model is adapted with low-rank modules to interaction concepts, and a second model predicts object pose sequences conditioned on human movement. This couples body motion with how an object may move over time. The generated examples address scarce interaction data, but video and lifting errors can enter the learned model. Plausible human–object motion is not itself a guaranteed mechanically valid robot interaction.
nodes.example: Condition on a target object and inspect the generated human motion together with the object trajectory. Check contact timing and geometry, and distinguish successful synthetic reconstruction from a physically executed interaction.
nodes.role_en: Couples object motion to human interaction. Course-associated reading for Beyond Plausible: Physically Valid Human-Object Interaction for Robot World Models.

nodes.summary: Dexterous World Models：以手部动作为条件的视频世界
nodes.definition: Dexterous World Models conditions video diffusion on a static scene rendering and an egocentric hand-motion sequence. Camera-following scene renderings provide spatial context, while rendered hand meshes encode the intended action. A hybrid dataset combines aligned synthetic interaction with real object-dynamics examples. The output is a video depicting plausible hand–scene effects, adding interactivity to otherwise static digital twins. Its observation-generation interface differs from a contact solver or torque controller; visual plausibility and physical executability must remain separate claims.
nodes.example: Render the same scene with two hand-motion conditions and compare generated object responses. Inspect camera consistency and contact appearance, then ask separately whether any resulting object trajectory is validated by a physics model or a real experiment.
nodes.role_en: Predicts visually plausible scene responses. Course-associated reading for Beyond Plausible: Physically Valid Human-Object Interaction for Robot World Models.

nodes.definition: HOPE predicts time-varying normal pressure and contact on a hand mesh from monocular video. Training maps heterogeneous tactile-glove, planar-pressure, and contact annotations into a shared hand-vertex space. A vertex-anchored video Transformer maintains persistent geometric tokens, and a contact-gated pressure head suppresses force estimates where contact is unlikely. This provides a common output interface independent of object shape or sensor layout. Vision-based pressure remains an inferred physical quantity, so calibration and pressure error need evaluation beyond contact classification.
nodes.example: Observe a hand squeezing or touching an object and inspect pressure on the same mesh vertices over time. Compare predicted contact and pressure against available sensor labels separately, because detecting touch does not determine its magnitude.
nodes.role_en: Separates likely contact from estimated force magnitude. Course-associated reading for Beyond Plausible: Physically Valid Human-Object Interaction for Robot World Models.

nodes.summary: RoFacto：机器人渲染接口与场景响应预测
nodes.definition: RoFacto factors robot-specific action realization and appearance out of a video world model. A command sequence runs through the robot controller and kinematics without scene contact to obtain a nominal trajectory, which is rendered using the robot description. The model then predicts scene response from this visual robot interface, static context, and geometric cues. The nominal rollout is available without future realized states, but it is not the true contact trajectory. This distinction prevents privileged future robot states from being mistaken for deployable input.
nodes.example: Run a command through the nominal robot model, render it, and predict the surrounding scene’s response. Compare with the actual contact rollout and test an unseen embodiment under the same rendering interface, without feeding future measured states into the predictor.
nodes.role_en: Supports contact and occlusion interpretation. Course-associated reading for Beyond Plausible: Physically Valid Human-Object Interaction for Robot World Models.

nodes.title: 双影深度线索
nodes.summary: Doubled contours, especially combined with blur, can contribute to perceived pictorial depth.
nodes.definition: This perception study asks whether doubled contours can communicate depth in an ordinary flat picture. When the eyes fixate one distance, objects elsewhere can produce two visible images; artists sometimes reproduce that appearance. nodes.en: Do Artists Use Linear Perspective to Depict Visual Space?
nodes.title: 艺术家如何画空间
nodes.summary: Artistic depictions systematically redistribute central and peripheral visual space.
nodes.definition: The paper compares artworks with photographs depicting the same scenes to examine how artists organize visual space. Its evidence includes paintings by the author, Cézanne landscapes, and drawings produced in a controlled study with art-trained participants. Across these sets, central regions tend to occupy more pictorial area while peripheral regions occupy less than in corresponding linear-perspective photographs. This is evidence about depiction strategies and their possible relationship to visual experience, rather than proof that every observer uses one universal alternative geometric projection.
nodes.example: Teaching example: compare a room photograph with a drawing from the same seat. Align the central object first, then inspect the surrounding walls. Enlarging the central object and compressing those walls changes the picture’s global geometry.
nodes.role_en: Artistic depictions systematically redistribute central and peripheral visual space.

nodes.summary: Examines the visible body as part of the observer’s visual field.
nodes.definition: Egocentric perspective here means depicting the scene that includes the observer’s own visible body from the observer’s viewpoint. The article discusses why familiar parts of experience, such as hands, legs, trunk, or nose, are often omitted from pictures and considers how artists can represent them. It connects bodily self-visibility with the composition of a visual field. It is a conceptual and artistic investigation; it does not recover body pose, learn an egocentric action model, or supply a quantitative robotics benchmark.

nodes.en: TIPS: Text-Image Pretraining with Spatial Awareness
nodes.title: 空间感知图文预训练
nodes.summary: Combines richer captions and masked-image learning for spatially useful image–text features.
nodes.definition: TIPS trains image and text encoders so one representation can support both image-level recognition and spatially detailed tasks. It combines image–text contrastive learning with masked-image self-supervision, rather than asking global caption matching alone to teach patch geometry. It also mixes original web captions with richer synthetic descriptions. These choices encourage local visual coherence while retaining language alignment. After pretraining, image features can be used by dense and global task protocols. The method produces representations; an appropriate downstream interface still determines how they become task outputs.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a caption says “dog outdoors,” while a richer description mentions the dog beside a fence. Contrastive supervision aligns language and image; a masked-patch objective also pressures the encoder to preserve local structure useful for segmentation.
nodes.role_en: Combines richer captions and masked-image learning for spatially useful image–text features.

nodes.en: TIPSv2: Advancing Vision-Language Pretraining with Enhanced Patch-Text Alignment
nodes.title: 增强图文局部对齐
nodes.summary: Improves patch–text alignment through iBOT++, head-only EMA, and multigranularity captions.
nodes.definition: TIPSv2 improves vision–language pretraining by investigating why distilled students can align image patches with text better than their teachers. Its revised recipe extends the patch self-supervision objective to all tokens through iBOT++, uses an exponential moving average on heads to reduce training overhead, and adds captions at multiple descriptive granularities. The output remains a general image–text encoder rather than a full scene parser. The central lesson is that pretraining objectives and teacher design shape local semantic alignment, even when global image retrieval already looks strong.
nodes.example: Teaching example: query the patch features of a street image with “bicycle wheel.” Improved patch–text alignment can highlight the wheel instead of the entire bicycle. This probes localized semantics, while the complete image embedding can still support retrieval.

nodes.en: HAMMR: HierArchical MultiModal React Agents for Generic VQA
nodes.title: 分层多模态工具智能体
nodes.summary: Uses specialized subagents to compose tools across varied VQA tasks.
nodes.definition: HAMMR organizes visual question answering as a hierarchy of multimodal reasoning-and-action agents. A higher-level agent can delegate to specialized agents, which use tools suited to subtasks such as counting, reading text, locating objects, or retrieving knowledge. This reduces the difficulty of selecting from a large undifferentiated tool menu for every question. Intermediate observations return through the hierarchy before an answer is produced. The system targets broad VQA coverage with one orchestration framework, while its reliability still depends on the tools, prompts, and delegation decisions used at inference.
nodes.example: Teaching example: answer “How many red packages have a price below five dollars?” One specialist locates and counts packages, another reads price labels, and the coordinating agent combines their observations. Errors in either specialist can affect the final count.

nodes.definition: This work defines a benchmark for a single image embedding that supports fine-grained and instance-level retrieval across different visual domains. nodes.en: UDON: Universal Dynamic Online Distillation for Generic Image Representations
nodes.title: 通用表征在线蒸馏
nodes.summary: Distills domain specialists into one encoder with adaptive domain sampling.
nodes.definition: UDON trains a universal image embedding using knowledge from domain-specialist teachers. Rather than keeping many independent full models, it shares most parameters between teachers and student and trains them together. A dynamic domain sampler gives more attention to domains that learn slowly, addressing unequal difficulty and long-tail distributions. The student receives domain-specific supervision while retaining one inference interface. The contribution is a training strategy for retrieval representations; the teachers and sampling machinery support learning, while deployment can use the universal student to embed images from multiple domains.
nodes.example: Teaching example: landmark retrieval improves quickly, while a product domain with many rare classes improves slowly. UDON can allocate more batches to the latter and distill its specialist features into a single student used by the search service.
nodes.role_en: Distills domain specialists into one encoder with adaptive domain sampling.

nodes.en: VESSA: Video-based Object-centric Self-Supervised Adaptation for Visual Foundation Models
nodes.title: 物体视频自监督适配
nodes.summary: Adapts visual encoders using unlabeled multiview object videos.
nodes.definition: VESSA adapts a pretrained visual encoder to a new domain using short object-centric videos without category annotations. Different frames show the same object under changing viewpoints and capture conditions, supplying useful positive correspondence for self-distillation. The method carefully configures prediction heads and parameter-efficient adaptation so the encoder gains domain robustness without quickly degrading its pretrained representation. Evaluation measures downstream recognition after adaptation. This is continued representation learning from video observations, not a controller trained to manipulate the object or a guarantee that every unlabeled video improves the encoder.
nodes.example: Teaching example: collect short turntable videos of unfamiliar industrial parts. Frames show each part from several angles. Adapt the encoder using that shared identity signal, then evaluate classification separately to check whether useful distinctions survived the adaptation.
nodes.role_en: Adapts visual encoders using unlabeled multiview object videos.

nodes.en: Optimization of Rank Losses for Image Retrieval
nodes.title: 检索排序损失优化
nodes.summary: Optimizes retrieval metrics through robust rank surrogates and batch-gap correction.
nodes.definition: The paper addresses the mismatch between retrieval metrics and convenient minibatch training objectives. Metrics such as average precision depend on discrete ordering and on many database examples, making direct differentiation and minibatch approximation difficult. SupRank supplies a differentiable upper-bound surrogate for rank-based objectives, while an additional term reduces discrepancies between batch-level and full-dataset optimization. The framework covers ordinary and hierarchical retrieval, including graded relationships between categories. At inference, the trained encoder still produces embeddings that are ranked by similarity; the special machinery changes how those embeddings are learned.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a relevant landmark image ranks sixth rather than second. A pairwise distance loss may improve without fixing that rank. A rank-oriented objective instead connects learning more directly to the retrieval ordering that the evaluator scores.
nodes.role_en: Optimizes retrieval metrics through robust rank surrogates and batch-gap correction.

nodes.title: 变换鲁棒对抗样本
nodes.summary: Optimizes adversarial inputs over transformations rather than a single fixed view.
nodes.definition: Expectation over Transformation constructs adversarial inputs that remain effective across a specified distribution of viewing or capture transformations. Instead of optimizing a perturbation only on one fixed image, the procedure optimizes its expected effect under sampled transformations. The paper demonstrates digital examples and textured three-dimensional objects evaluated through physical capture. The attacked classifier need not learn new parameters; the optimized object or image is its input. Robustness is relative to the chosen transformation distribution and evaluation setup, so the demonstrations do not imply effectiveness against every camera, classifier, or environment.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a texture optimized for one front-facing photograph may fail after rotation. Optimizing across rendered viewpoints can make the same object misleading from several angles. Evaluation must still include held-out views and, for physical claims, actual camera captures.
nodes.role_en: Optimizes adversarial inputs over transformations rather than a single fixed view.

nodes.en: LAMP: Learning Universal Adversarial Perturbations for Multi-Image Tasks via Pre-trained Models
nodes.title: 多图通用对抗扰动
nodes.summary: Examines transferable universal perturbations that disrupt multi-image reasoning.
nodes.definition: LAMP studies attacks on models that reason over multiple images at once. It learns a reusable perturbation through accessible pretrained models and evaluates transfer to downstream multi-image systems. Its objectives target information aggregation across images, spread the effect of perturbed tokens to clean tokens, and reduce dependence on which image position is modified. This matters because an attacker may control only some images in a larger context. The paper’s black-box setting concerns the downstream target; optimization still relies on accessible surrogate models and an explicitly defined perturbation-learning setup.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a webpage assistant compares several product photographs, only one of which comes from an untrusted source. The research asks whether perturbing that image can disrupt reasoning about the whole set, including clean images placed later in context.
nodes.role_en: Examines transferable universal perturbations that disrupt multi-image reasoning.

nodes.en: SoundBreak: A Systematic Study of Audio-Only Adversarial Attacks on Trimodal Models
nodes.title: 三模态模型音频攻击
nodes.summary: Quantifies audio-only failure surfaces in audio–video–language systems.
nodes.definition: SoundBreak evaluates whether changing only an audio stream can disrupt models that jointly process audio, video, and language. The study compares objectives aimed at encoder features, attention, internal representations, and output likelihoods while leaving the other modalities unchanged. It also investigates environmental transformations through room-impulse-response simulation. Its results show that a single modality can undermine broader multimodal reasoning, but cross-model transfer remains limited. Reported simulated acoustic robustness is distinct from a completed loudspeaker-and-microphone deployment, and attack success must be read together with the perturbation and perceptual-quality conditions.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a clip’s video stays unchanged while its audio is modified. A trimodal assistant then answers the same question incorrectly. To interpret the failure, compare the clean answer, audio distortion, attack objective, and whether the evaluation used simulation or physical playback.
nodes.role_en: Quantifies audio-only failure surfaces in audio–video–language systems.

nodes.en: Immunizing Models Against Harmful Long-Horizon Fine-Tuning via Contractive Optimization Dynamics
nodes.title: 长期微调模型免疫
nodes.summary: Shapes harmful adaptation dynamics to limit long-horizon fine-tuning progress.
nodes.definition: CLAMP changes a model before release so that adaptation to a designated harmful task becomes difficult over long optimization horizons while benign utility remains useful. It models harmful fine-tuning updates as a dynamical process and encourages successive updates to contract. Under the stated assumptions, the remaining movement and harmful progress can be bounded from a finite simulated trajectory. A curvature penalty complements that progress objective. This is a model-immunization training method, not an inference-time content filter, and its guarantees are conditional on the optimization setting used in the analysis.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a defense that slows the first ten harmful fine-tuning steps may fail after thousands. CLAMP instead tries to make later harmful updates progressively smaller. Check long-run adaptation curves and benign-task utility before judging whether that objective helped.
nodes.role_en: Shapes harmful adaptation dynamics to limit long-horizon fine-tuning progress.

nodes.en: IntroConformal: Conformal Factuality Guarantees for Large Vision-Language Models via Introspective Signals
nodes.title: 视觉语言事实风险控制
nodes.summary: Calibrates introspective signals to filter factual claims with statistical risk control.
nodes.definition: IntroConformal filters claims from vision–language model outputs using confidence signals obtained from the model itself. It studies semantic stability across hidden layers and a self-verification probability, then calibrates a decision rule through conformal risk control. The base model does not require retraining, but calibration requires labeled factuality examples and a suitable exchangeability setting. The guarantee controls the specified statistical risk across future examples under its assumptions. It does not certify each individual retained sentence, eliminate distribution shift, or turn the model’s self-judgment into unquestionable evidence.
nodes.example: Teaching example: a model describes an image using several factual claims. Score each claim, calibrate the filtering threshold on annotated examples, and omit uncertain claims. A chosen population risk target still allows individual mistakes and may require abstention on difficult images.
nodes.role_en: Calibrates introspective signals to filter factual claims with statistical risk control.

edges.why_en: Adds dense-feature stabilization through patch Gram anchoring alongside further self-supervised scaling.
Self-distillation predicts teacher representations; masked autoencoding reconstructs missing pixels.
Extends image masking to spatiotemporal video tokens and tube masking.
Adds decoder-side token reduction to scale masked video training.
Both predict embeddings; block-masked context prediction and causal next-embedding prediction organize targets differently.
Changes batch-normalized contrastive softmax into pairwise sigmoid image–text matching.
Context tokens adapt a frozen image–text space to task-dependent categorizations.
Adds explicit local phrase-region agreement to global image–text alignment.
Moves from monocular teacher–student depth toward any-view spatially consistent depth-ray prediction.
Compresses inter-frame communication through registers and simplifies dense prediction for larger-scale geometry training.
Joint multi-head geometric prediction and unified depth-ray targets are different ways to encode spatial reconstruction.
Dense supervised geometric learning and self-supervised explicit reconstruction differ in their training evidence.
Geometry-aware ray position encoding can improve multi-view attention; this link expresses the component/task relationship, not a claim of identical code.
Both use Gaussian maps; LatentAM emphasizes compact semantic features and online dictionaries rather than only RGB-D tracking/rendering.
Explicit relational graphs and continuous 3D latent maps supply different persistent context interfaces.
Latent map-conditioned action and language-rich 4D graph reasoning use spatial memory for different outputs.
Dynamics-constrained implicit geometry and generative shape completion use contact evidence through different inference mechanisms.
Material/light inverse rendering and progressive visual–physical optimization solve related but distinct inverse problems.
Sparse multi-view progressive fitting and monocular visual–physical coupling address different observation constraints.
The information criterion used to design interactions can also rank recorded contact data.
One refines a simulator through informative real data; the other transfers exploration even when direct task-policy transfer fails.
Posterior-aware pretraining and frozen-policy latent steering act at different stages of policy improvement.
Learned spatial tool coordination and interruptible physical orchestration address related tool-use problems with different timing requirements.
Both require interaction to reveal hidden evidence; answering a question and retrieving a target are distinct task objectives.
Replaces a cascaded VAE/representation interface with simple pixel-patch embeddings and end-to-end learning.
A shared mixed-loss Transformer and a query bridge to a diffusion decoder offer distinct understanding/generation integrations.
Adds explicit open-vocabulary semantic part control to shape generation.
Adds independent per-part spatial layout control to compositional generation.
Both generate assets through programs; domain-specific articulation tests and typed assembly mates expose different structural interfaces.
Human motion diffusion becomes an online planner for a feedback-controlled simulated character.
Adapted human motion diffusion supplies an interaction-conditioned component of dynamic affordance generation.
Both connect generative motion to control; their simulated-character and physical-humanoid systems have different execution evidence.
Internal temporal memory and explicit experience-keyframe retrieval provide different ways to retain task history.
Hierarchical instruction-producing retrieval differs from a memory-bank-conditioned diffusion action expert.
The benchmark taxonomy explains which history-dependent capabilities a memory policy should be evaluated for; it is not an assertion of one shared implementation.
Both learn world/action representations; VTAM adds tactile futures and avoids full video denoising at action inference.
Generated 3D human–object motion and hand-conditioned interaction video represent affordances at different output levels.
Both exploit rendered actor geometry; RoFacto additionally factors command realization through a robot controller/kinematics interface.
Temporal tactile policy encoding and video–tactile future learning differ in how touch supports action.

research.title: Three-session primary-source audit
research.scope: Nineteen scheduled readings associated with Robert Pepperell, André Araujo, and Chris Thomas; relations are reading-list associations, not proof of authorship or delivery.
findings: All nineteen titles resolved to primary publication, author project, or institutional author records.

The listed Synthesizing Robust Adversarial Examples repository is a third-party reproducibility-challenge implementation, explicitly not the original author repository. The original is Athalye, Engstrom, Ilyas, and Kwok, ICML 2018; it is not a Chris Thomas paper.
IntroConformal, initially unlinked, resolves to arXiv 2609.01375 and EMNLP 2026 ACL Anthology 2026.emnlp-main.2585.
Immunizing Models... has a CVPR 2026 publication as well as a separate same-title Virginia Tech thesis; the thesis record alone must not define paper authorship.
Sound-Break is normalized to the primary title SoundBreak. Its room-response experiments are simulations, not proof of real acoustic playback.
Fovography belongs to IC3D 2017 but the institutional proceedings record gives 2018-01-11 publication.
Pepperell entries are perceptual experiments, artistic analysis, or imaging frameworks. No neural-network architectures or robot evaluation claims were inferred.
Exact neural parameter counts, uninspected participant counts, and exhaustive training-data sizes are omitted rather than guessed.
All equations are explicitly labeled teaching schematics, not original-paper equation quotations.
